meta.title: Eduversal Academic Standards — Section Ownership by School Appraisal Domain
meta.purpose: Assigns every one of the 24 Eduversal Academic Standards sections to exactly one owning School Appraisal domain, so that each domain’s two Academic Board members have a named, non-overlapping review remit over the corpus.
meta.ownershipModel: Five domains × two Academic Board members = ten reviewers. The lead signs off the domain; the second reviewer reads independently before sign-off. Ownership means accountability for the accuracy, currency and internal consistency of those sections — it does not confer sole authorship: corpus edits still follow the three-step ES pipeline (Academic Hub/Sections → build-academic-standards.js → mirror-research-to-hubs.js).
meta.relationshipToFrameworkAnchors: This file is NOT the same thing as school-appraisal-framework.json → domains[].frameworkAnchors.eduversalStandardRefs. Those anchors name the standards that substantively ground a domain’s ratings and render as ES chips in the appraisal UI; they are curated and legitimately omit appendix material. This file is a complete partition: all 24 sections, appendices included, each with exactly one owner. The two were reconciled on 2026-08-23 and should not be allowed to drift apart silently.
meta.splitSections: Section 15 (50 maddes) is the one section deliberately split across two domains. It is nearly twice the size of the next-largest section and divides cleanly at subsection-block level into risk governance (D1) and pastoral / campus safety (D5). No other section is shared.
sources: docs/research/eduversal/academic-standards/section-24.json → 24.7 — Cambridge examinations administration is assessed through D3, with the authoritative detail in Sections 3 and 10
docs/research/eduversal/academic-standards/section-24.json → 24.3 — CIS Domain D7–D8 records that assessment straddles D2 (methods, feedback) and D4 (achievement data, reporting)
maintenance: When a section is added to or retired from the ES corpus, add or remove it here in the same pass — an unowned section is the failure mode this file exists to prevent.
When an appraisal domain is renamed or re-scoped, re-check every assignment; ES 24.9 already requires the same re-check of the 24.2 domain list.
When an owner changes, update owners[] here rather than tracking the roster in a spreadsheet or a G-Doc. This file is the roster of record.
Owner names are intentionally null on first commit — populate them before the assignment is announced to the Board.

sharedSections.title: Assessment and Reporting
sharedSections.note: Section 6 straddles two domains by design — ES 24.3 records that CIS places assessment methods and feedback quality under D2 while achievement data and reporting fall under D4. Ownership sits with D4: the section is titled Assessment AND Reporting, and 6.8–6.10 plus 6.14–6.15 are reporting and external-assessment maddes. D2’s pair is consulted on 6.5–6.7 and 6.11, which are classroom-assessment practice.

sharedSections.title: Risk Management, Emergency Preparedness, and Business Continuity
sharedSections.note: Split at subsection-block level; see each domain’s partial-scope entry. Note that ES chips cannot express this split: data-es-ref accepts a whole-section number or a real madde id, and a subsection-level ref such as "15.2" is absent from manifest.maddeIndex and would render as a phantom ref. Section 15 therefore appears whole on both D1 and D5 in frameworkAnchors.
